subject: CatalystHealth latency acceptance runway & checklist
messages:
From: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>
To: Aliya Rahman <aliya@catalysthealth.com>; CatalystHealth Product Ops <productops@catalysthealth.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-04-03T15:12:00-07:00
Subject: CatalystHealth latency acceptance runway & checklist

Hi Aliya / Product Ops team,

Thanks again for the time today — good discussion on the integration surface and your performance targets. As promised, I captured the follow-ups and a focused checklist to align on p95/p99 end-to-end targets for the hosted option vs your incumbent provider. Please see the short runway below and let me know where you'd like to prioritize validation.

Quick recap (from call):
- Workload: document summarization + clinical triage assistant (batch size ~1, avg tokens 280).
- Expected peak QPS: 12 writes/sec sustained during clinic hours; spike to 28 QPS on batch windows.
- Streaming: token-by-token acknowledgements required for UI progressive render (must keep first-byte latency low).
- Current p95/p99 (incumbent): p95 = 220ms, p99 = 950ms for single-turn requests (measured end-to-end through your proxy).
- Target acceptance for switch to hosted: p95 <= 220ms (match) and p99 <= 1.1s (must not exceed incumbent by >150ms) under production-like traffic.

Naomi's proposed next steps (short runway):
1) Align test harness inputs — we need two representative traffic traces from you (steady and peak window).
2) Redwood will run two hosted probes: a baseline (no KV caching) and an optimized run (prefix caching + 8-concurrency batching).
3) We provide a draft SLA clause and a latency-acceptance worksheet for your procurement/legal to review.
4) Schedule a 2-hour lab session next week for a live streaming check (tokenization + first-byte SLOs).

I've attached a working SLO matrix and a draft SLA (see attachments). Items I need from you to proceed:
- Representative traces (jsonl) or replay script by EOD Friday
- Confirmation on production-like concurrency profile (we discussed 6 workers with 4 streams each)
- Any hard ceiling on p99 beyond the numbers above

If you prefer, Ben can own the probe execution and Laura will coordinate contract language.

Best,

Naomi Feldman
Senior Sales Engineer | Redwood Inference
naomi.feldman@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0192

Attachments: catalyst_slo_matrix_v2.xlsx (spreadsheet), hosted-latency-sla-draft.pdf (text)
From: Aliya Rahman <aliya@catalysthealth.com>

Cc: Product Ops <productops@catalysthealth.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-04-03T18:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: CatalystHealth latency acceptance runway & checklist

Hi Naomi — thanks for the clear write-up. Quick answers inline: 

- We can share a small replay trace (steady, 5k reqs) and a 30-min peak snapshot by Friday COB. Will send links to the traces (S3 signed URLs).
- Concurrency confirmation: production will look like 6 app workers x up to 6 streaming sessions each (we can synthesize this in the harness).
- p99 ceiling: procurement prefers not to see p99 exceed 1.2s; engineering would consider 1.1s acceptable if variability is small.

Action items on our side:
- Product Ops to generate traces (I assigned to them)
- Security will need the latency probe scope for the private endpoints (if any) — I copied our security lead form here in case baseline certs are needed later.

We like the idea of a 2-hour lab. Can you propose two slots next week? Prefer morning Pacific.

Thanks,

—Aliya
Director, Product Platform
CatalystHealth
aliya@catalysthealth.com

Hi Aliya — happy to pick this up.

Proposed lab slots (Pacific):
- Tuesday 2027-04-06 09:00–11:00 PT
- Wednesday 2027-04-07 10:00–12:00 PT

Plan for the 2-hour session:
- 0–20m: quick sync on traffic replay and endpoints (confirm headers, auth).
- 20–60m: baseline run (hosted default config). We capture p50/p95/p99 and first-byte distribution for streaming.
- 60–100m: optimized run (prefix caching + batching tweaks; up to 8 concurrency per worker).
- 100–120m: recap, next steps, and scheduling of a longer soak if needed.

We will bring the hosted probe harness and a small dashboard snapshot for live metrics. If you can include the S3 traces in advance we can pre-stage them to reduce setup time.

Laura — can you please drop the draft SLA clause into the shared drive and invite Aliya? I'll attach the exact probe command we run so their infra team can review.

Ben Carter
